event.marcus_heart2.0.text: Hold this end a moment, [player]. Don't level it. Just hold it.
event.marcus_heart2.0.why: asks for the smallest help; trust measured in a plank

event.marcus_heart2.1.text: Measure once. Twice. ...Three times, my father said. Level as a lake.
event.marcus_heart2.1.why: signature bit; the praise is in the measurement

event.marcus_heart2.2.text: Take these. Leftovers from the big jobs. None long enough for the hall roof. I checked.
event.marcus_heart2.2.why: gift plus the roof thread, understated

event.marcus_heart5.0.text: I carved this when I was nine. A barn, about the size of a fist.

event.marcus_heart5.1.text: Silly, perhaps. The doors don't open. I glued them shut in a hurry. I want you to have it.
event.marcus_heart5.1.why: the one thing he rushed, handed over

event.marcus_heart5.2.text: Keep your tools sharp, friend. The bag is for your fields. Some things are allowed to hurry.
event.marcus_heart5.2.why: explains the speed fertilizer and forgives the hurry

event.hall_dance.0.text: I checked the roof once. Twice. ...Three times, my father said. It is finished. Not nearly. Finished.

event.hall_dance.11.text: One coin. One dance. I measured this floor for it. Twice.
event.hall_dance.11.why: drops Bram's 'Hm'; the dance as a measured job

event.story_pie_payoff.intro.text: [player]. A word, quietly. You know the way to the clinic, don't you?
event.story_pie_payoff.intro.why: conspiratorial ask, names the target without naming her

dlg.story.pie.talk.0.text: One slice of my pie. Her door. No name. If she asks, a stranger with excellent taste.

dlg.story.pie.talk.1.text: Well? You can say no. I'll just stand here holding it.

dlg.story.pie.talk.c1.text: I'll improve it on the way.

dlg.story.pie.talk.c2.text: It might not survive the walk.
dlg.story.pie.talk.c2.why: funniest last; still means eat it

dlg.story.pie.talk.r0.text: You leave the slice on Odalys's step. She reads the note, sighs, and takes a bite.

dlg.story.pie.talk.r1.text: You add a pinch of cinnamon on the way. Odalys tastes it, then frowns at it for a long time.

dlg.story.pie.talk.r2.text: You eat the slice on the road. It is excellent. Two bakers will hear about this.

event.story_pie_payoff.after.text: {if choice:pie.honest}'Rather good.' She said 'rather good.' Don't repeat it. I'll repeat it enough.{else}{if choice:pie.improve}She sent a note back: 'Cinnamon? Cheek.' Best review I've ever had.{else}You ate it. Fair. Now she's baking a second, and so am I. Ambitiously.{/if}{/if}
event.story_pie_payoff.after.why: each branch lands on his own word; 'ambitious' callback

event.story_whistler_marcus.intro.text: Ah. You've found me. I whistle when the grain runs true. It's running very true tonight.
event.story_whistler_marcus.intro.why: drops the stage direction from his mouth; confession as craft

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.0.text: It's a family tune. My grandfather hit one note wrong, and we've all kept it since.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.1.text: ...Well? Go on. Everybody has an opinion about the note.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.c0.text: Say hello, like a normal neighbor.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.c2.text: Say nothing. Wait for the encore.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r0.text: Hello. Yes. Hello. Thank you for the normal approach. It's rarer than you'd think.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r1.text: You got the wrong note exactly right. I'm moved. Also mortified.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r2.text: You listened. All of it. ...Grandfather would have liked you. I may whistle again. Quietly.

event.story_whistler_marcus.after.text: A wrong note is only wrong if you apologize for it. Wednesdays, I whistle on the bench. Bram pretends not to hear.
event.story_whistler_marcus.after.why: proverb plus a place and day to visit

event.story_pumpkin_marcus.intro.text: Ah. You've found out. A practice lantern. I measured the face twice. Never asked whose pumpkin.

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.0.text: Behind the store, Marcus stands beside a very large pumpkin with a very guilty face.

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.2.text: ...It might be. It has a nose now.

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.c2.why: funniest last; still means help carry

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r1.text: An apology. Yes. I'm sorry, Tilda. Truly. And sorry to you, pumpkin. You deserved a plan.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r1.why: apologizes to the work, in character

event.story_pumpkin_marcus.after.text: It goes back with a face carved in. Tilda calls it an improvement. I've stopped trying not to smile.
event.story_pumpkin_marcus.after.why: first person; was third person in his own mouth

event.marcus_heart8.intro.text: Come in. I want you to see the roof plan. Not many have. I measure twice. You look once.

dlg.marcus.roof.0.text: Pitch, rafters, shingles. Drawn nine times. Every time it looks right. Every time I'm afraid it won't hold.

dlg.marcus.roof.1.text: Six winters, it's been nearly fixed. ...What would you do?

dlg.marcus.roof.c2.text: I'll hold the ladder. I'm good at holding.

dlg.marcus.roof.r0.text: Measure with me. Yes. You take the end of the tape. Once. Twice. ...Three times.

dlg.marcus.roof.r1.text: A new pitch. I'd stopped asking that question. ...Show me the angle. Slowly.

dlg.marcus.roof.r2.text: The ladder. Plain, steady, necessary. Best offer I've had in six winters.

event.marcus_heart8.after.text: {if choice:roof.measure}You measured with me. Three times, the last under your breath. First time I haven't been alone with it.{else}{if choice:roof.design}A steeper pitch. I'd never have tried it. I'll draw it tonight. Not nine times. Perhaps four.{else}You held the ladder. That's half of any building. The roof's still nearly fixed. Less nearly, now.{/if}{/if}
event.marcus_heart8.after.why: each branch ends on its truest word

event.marcus_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. I planed a plank for it, like every year. A straight board. Sit, if you like.

dlg.marcus.birthday.c2.text: Need someone on the other end?

dlg.marcus.birthday.r0.text: Thank you. I'll write it on the beam, small. Measure twice, thank twice.

dlg.marcus.birthday.r1.text: Oak. Straight grain, no knots. Thank you for noticing. Most people see a board.

dlg.marcus.birthday.r2.text: The other end. Yes. A second pair of hands is the best present there is.

event.marcus_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.marcus.wish}It's on the beam now, in small letters. That beam will outlast us both.{else}{if choice:bday.marcus.plank}You noticed the plank. Nobody notices. It's going up over the door.{else}Two hands on one plank. A quiet birthday. A good one.{/if}{/if}
event.marcus_birthday.after.why: a building that outlives him, kept small

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_1.l1.text: Dorian. Hold the end. No, the other end. ...There.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_1.l3.text: Straight. That's the whole job. I couldn't have said it shorter.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_2.l1.text: An hour, and you haven't said a word.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_2.l3.text: I nearly got worried. Then I didn't. Best hour of the week.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_3.l1.text: I hung a new door on your room. Oak. Heavier than it looks, like most things.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_3.l1.why: understatement that could be about either of them

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_3.l3.text: That's all a door is for. Closing on purpose.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l1.text: Dorian. I built a window for your room. Square. Oak. Measured three times.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l1.why: the third measure means it matters

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l3.text: Facing the owl. You two can finally be introduced.

event.overheard_bram_marcus_1.l2.text: Your weld's clean. Don't tell Juno I said so.

event.overheard_bram_marcus_1.l4.text: Good. Hand me the clamp. Wednesday, same bench.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_1.l4.why: the friendship as a standing appointment

event.overheard_bram_marcus_2.l2.text: Made you one. Oak. Measured your grip twice while you weren't looking.

event.overheard_bram_marcus_3.l2.text: A hundred and four. All straight. Counted twice.

event.overheard_bram_marcus_3.l4.text: Measure them. Bring them Wednesday. Lunch goes to the straighter.

event.overheard_marcus_odalys_2.l1.text: Dr. Penn. The bench outside your clinic had a loose leg. It's fixed.

event.overheard_marcus_odalys_2.l3.text: That's why it worked loose. Nobody sits on it. Five minutes would do it good.

event.overheard_marcus_odalys_3.l2.text: Better. I rest it Wednesdays. The doctor told me to.
event.overheard_marcus_odalys_3.l2.why: specific day; she can answer 'I did'

event.overheard_marcus_odalys_3.l4.text: Then take your own advice. Saturdays. I'll build the chair.
event.overheard_marcus_odalys_3.l4.why: Saturday is her day off in canon, not Sunday

adds.text: Most hands drift. Yours stayed put. That's rarer than good oak.
adds.why: the actual compliment, in craft terms

adds.text: My father said a thing done fast stays done wrong. He kept it on his shelf anyway.
adds.why: the root of measuring three times, and the love under it

adds.text: Edmund had a door that never opened, too. His cellar. He wouldn't let me oil it.
adds.why: doors rhyme; points at the cellar-door thread without explaining it

threads.marcus_heart2: The hall roof: the leftovers are 'not long enough', so what would be?
threads.marcus_heart5: Edmund's cellar door, the one he would not let Marcus oil.
threads.hall_dance: The roof is finished at last; what does Marcus build next, now nothing is 'nearly'?
threads.story_pie_payoff: The pie feud is not over: someone is always baking a second.
threads.story_whistler_marcus: Wednesdays on the bench: Marcus whistles, Bram pretends not to hear.
threads.story_pumpkin_marcus: Whether Tilda puts the pumpkin, or Marcus, on her slate.
threads.marcus_heart8: The roof is still 'nearly fixed', but now the player is part of it.
threads.marcus_birthday: The beam with the small letters, meant to outlast them both.
threads.overheard_marcus_dorian_2: What else the two lodgers are building in all that quiet.
threads.overheard_marcus_dorian_3: Whether Dorian's new door stays open, mostly.
threads.overheard_marcus_dorian_4: The owl outside Dorian's window, still waiting for a name.
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_1: Wednesday on the bench, and the compliment Juno must not hear.
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_2: The new hammer handle, made to a grip measured in secret.
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_3: Whose nails are straighter, settled Wednesday over lunch.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_1: Whether Marcus will actually bend his knees.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_2: Whether Dr. Penn sits on the mended bench for her five minutes.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_3: The chair Marcus will build so the doctor rests on Saturdays.

notes: hall_dance: Wren says 'Seven winters of coins'; canon is six winters (I use six in heart8). Please fix Wren's line or confirm.
hall_dance narration 'Tilda lets him lead' describes two people dancing together, which the brief forbids; suggest 'Marcus takes his one dance. Tilda dances beside him.'
hall_dance.11 dropped 'Hm.': that is Bram's tic.
story_whistler_marcus.intro had a stage direction inside Marcus's line; removed. Director may want a narration beat for the plank.
story_pumpkin_marcus.after was written in third person ('Marcus will not stop smiling') though Marcus speaks it; rewritten first person.
overheard_marcus_odalys_3.l4 said 'Sundays'; Dr. Penn's clinic closes Saturday, so changed to 'Saturdays'.
Kept unchanged: dlg.marcus.birthday.0 (shipped line), overheard_bram_marcus_2.l4, overheard_marcus_odalys_1.l4.
